summary.headline: The Regional School Committee appointed Kate Clark as Student Support Services Director and voted to withdraw from School Choice for 2026-2027.
summary.summary: At its April 15 meeting, the Regional School Committee held a public hearing and voted unanimously to withdraw from the state School Choice program for the 2026-2027 school year due to capacity and cost disparities. The committee approved the appointment of Kate Clark as the district's Director of Student Support Services following a staff departure. Members also reviewed elective enrollment trends following recent graduation requirement revisions, discussed school food service operations and cell phone legislation, and honored three departing long-time committee members.

topics.title: School Choice public hearing and opt-out vote
topics.summary: The superintendent opened a public hearing recommending that the district withdraw from the state School Choice program for the 2026-2027 school year. He cited a financial disparity between the $5,000 state tuition reimbursement received versus Algonquin's per-pupil operating cost of $25,042, as well as concerns that taking outside students would exceed target class size caps. The committee held the hearing without public comment and later voted unanimously to opt out.
key_details: State tuition reimbursement is $5,000 per student versus Algonquin per-pupil cost of $25,042.
Opting out protects local class size policies across grades.
The committee voted unanimously to withdraw from school choice for the 2026-2027 academic year.
topics.outcome: Voted unanimously to opt out of the School Choice program for 2026-2027.
topics.why_it_matters: Participating in school choice impacts district class sizes and shifts the financial burden onto member towns Northborough and Southborough when tuition receipts fall far short of education costs.

topics.title: Recognition of student and departing committee members
topics.summary: The committee honored senior Laura White for her photography and selection to the 2026 All-New England Journalism Staff by the New England Scholastic Press Association. The committee and administration also recognized three departing committee members for their service: Paul Desmond (served since 2017), Sean O'Shea (served since 2019), and Chris Covino (served since 2020).
key_details: Laura White was one of only 17 students selected across New England for journalism photography honors.
Paul Desmond served since 2017 across K-8 and regional committees.
Sean O'Shea served on the regional committee since May 2019.
Chris Covino served on the committee since 2020.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved open meeting minutes from March 18, 2026, and Audit Sub-Committee minutes from March 9, 2026. Members also voted to accept three community donations totaling $2,200, acknowledged student publications awards, reviewed the personnel report, and adjourned.
key_details: Accepted $1,000 donation from Sterling Chu for varsity math team letters.
Accepted $1,000 donation from Diana Nicklaus of SAAM Architecture for the DECA program.
Accepted a $200 Wegmans gift card donation for the METG theatre celebration.
Acknowledged a one-year leave of absence for staff member Colleen Smith.
Noted Silver Crown honors for The Harbinger and Gold Crown honors for Sachem.

topics.title: Appointment of Director of Student Support Services
topics.summary: The superintendent recommended appointing Kate Clark as the Director of Student Support Services for the Northborough-Southborough Regional School District, succeeding Helene Desjardins, who accepted a position in Hopkinton. Clark has served as assistant director at Algonquin since 2019. The restructuring places dedicated support directors in each district rather than a single overarching director across all three local school districts.
key_details: Helene Desjardins is departing to serve as student services director in Hopkinton.
Kate Clark has worked as assistant director at Algonquin since 2019.
District restructured the position to assign a director specifically to the regional district.
Appointment is subject to successful contract negotiations.
topics.outcome: Appointed Kate Clark as Director of Student Support Services, pending contract negotiations.

topics.title: State legislative update and cell phone restrictions
topics.summary: The superintendent updated the committee on state budget drafts and legislative efforts regarding bell-to-bell cell phone bans and restrictions on social media for youth under age 14. Minimum Chapter 70 aid is trending favorably in the House budget proposal at $160 per student, up from $145. The administration noted that state legislation mandating schoolwide cell phone bans could take effect in the 2026-2027 school year, prompting preparations for district implementation.
key_details: State House budget proposal sets minimum Chapter 70 aid at $160 per student.
Legislation proposing bell-to-bell cell phone bans in public schools is advancing.
District staff are researching logistical and technology solutions used in other districts such as Watertown.
topics.outcome: Information presented with no committee action taken.

topics.title: Social Studies Department presentation
topics.summary: Social Studies Department Chair Brittany Burns presented a department overview, highlighting course enrollments, Universal Design for Learning initiatives, and civic engagement. Enrollments in Advanced Placement courses continue to rise, with 80 sophomores enrolled in AP U.S. History and over a third of juniors enrolled in AP World History. She also highlighted new partnerships with the American Heritage Museum in Hudson and peer teaching visits between high schoolers and elementary students.
key_details: 14 teachers in the department collectively hold over 283 years of experience at Algonquin.
80 sophomores enrolled in AP U.S. History and 115 juniors in AP World History (rising to 136 next year).
Universal Design for Learning (UDL) instructional methods are being led schoolwide by department faculty.
Sophomores are piloting a field-study program with the American Heritage Museum in Hudson.

topics.title: Food services update
topics.summary: Administration reported on the ninth month of the district food service management contract with Whitsons Culinary Group. Lunch participation increased to 67 percent while breakfast dropped slightly to 13 percent, and higher food and labor costs have impacted the program during the stabilization period. Staffing changes occurred with the onboarding of food service director Linda St. Hilaire in November 2025, and popular menu items including freshly baked cookies have been reformulated to meet state nutrition rules.
key_details: Lunch participation increased from 65% to 67%; breakfast participation decreased from 14% to 13%.
Linda St. Hilaire was hired as food service director in November 2025.
A formal recommendation on Year 2 of the Whitsons contract will be presented in May.
Third-lunch shortages earlier in the year were traced to supply chain disruptions from a blizzard.
topics.outcome: Report accepted; contract renewal recommendation scheduled for next month.

topics.title: Personal finance graduation requirement discussion
topics.summary: A committee member reported on a Massachusetts Association of School Committees webinar regarding pending state legislation (House Bill 4670) to establish a personal financial literacy requirement. Principal Sean Bevan clarified that Algonquin already mandates a semester of economics or financial literacy to graduate, and that the school is introducing an AP Business and Personal Finance course next year. The committee discussed distinctions between broader macroeconomic financial literacy and personal budgeting skills.
key_details: Pending Massachusetts House Bill 4670 would require personal financial literacy instruction in middle or high school.
Algonquin already requires students to complete one semester of economics or financial literacy.
A new AP Business and Personal Finance course will be offered in the 2026-2027 school year.

topics.title: Student and Principal reports on Program of Studies changes
topics.summary: Student representative Maddie presented results from a 52-student advisory survey on academic stress, cafeteria options, and school climate. Principal Sean Bevan followed with a detailed review of course enrollment shifts resulting from the committee's decision to drop digital literacy as a mandatory graduation requirement. Freed elective space led incoming freshmen to disperse across diverse subjects, including sharp increases in nutrition, business fundamentals, psychology, early childhood development, ceramics, and ensemble music.
key_details: Digital literacy was reduced from 16 sections (299 students) to likely one section of roughly 10 students for 2026-2027.
Top freshman elective enrollments include Nutrition/Culinary Arts, Business Fundamentals, Psychology, and Early Childhood Development.
Enrollments in symphonic band and concert choir grew after schedule flexibility increased and the fine arts requirement doubled.
The new AP Business and Personal Finance course saw high enrollment, especially among male upperclassmen.
Student survey feedback highlighted stress peaks around midterms and requested additional gender-neutral bathrooms.
topics.why_it_matters: Recent changes to graduation requirements have shifted student course choices away from mandatory computer literacy toward arts, business, and music electives, directly impacting high school scheduling and staffing.

topics.title: FY26 budget transfers and financial reporting
topics.summary: The committee reviewed year-to-date FY26 budget figures and approved line-item budget transfers. As of March 31, 2026, the district has $441,366 remaining in its operating budget, or approximately 1.49 percent. Four line items experienced overages: professional development substitutes, athletic trainer additions, winter snow and ice removal, and special education translation services.
key_details: Operating budget has $441,366 unencumbered (1.49% of budget) three-quarters through FY26.
Budget transfers addressed deficits in snow removal, athletics, PD substitutes, and special education translation.
Total revenue receipts reached 74% of the annual estimate as of March 31.
topics.outcome: Voted unanimously to approve the FY26 budget line-item transfers, general fund expenditure report, and statement of revenue.

topics.title: Religious and cultural observance policy review
topics.summary: The superintendent and committee members discussed Policy I-340 regarding religious and cultural observances following community feedback received during Passover. School leaders emphasized that while policy exists to excuse students from assignments and exams on major holidays, adherence has been inconsistent among teaching staff. The administration plans proactive, districtwide calendar notifications and goal-setting reminders to ensure students are accommodated without penalty.
key_details: District received parent feedback reporting that policy provisions were not consistently followed during recent religious holidays.
Policy I-340 requires accommodations for students observing religious holidays without academic penalty.
Administrators will implement advance reminder notices and incorporate policy adherence into annual staff communication.
topics.outcome: Referred to the policy subcommittee and administration for improved communication and enforcement.

votes.motion: Approve open meeting minutes of March 18, 2026 and Audit Sub-Committee minutes of March 9, 2026.
Appoint Kate Clark as Director of Student Support Services for the Northborough-Southborough Regional School District pending successful contract negotiations.
Withdraw from the School Choice program for the 2026-2027 academic year.
Approve donations of $1,000 from Sterling Chu for the math team, $1,000 from Diana Nicklaus for DECA, and a $200 Wegmans gift card for METG theatre.
Approve the FY26 budget line-item transfers and the monthly general fund expenditure report.
Approve the FY26 Statement of Revenue as presented.
